points.label: Covenant setting
points.left: The first explicit covenant language in the biblical sequence appears inside a judgment-and-preservation scene rather than after the danger has passed.
points.right: The parties, scope, sign, and repeated promise not to destroy all flesh by flood are all stated in the scene itself.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: God establishes · Noah · household · Enter ark · preserve life · Covenant announced before fulfillment
points.right: God establishes · remembers · Noah · descendants · every living creature · Rainbow sign · Waters will not again become a flood to destroy all flesh

payload.posture: Genesis 6 announces establishment before the flood; Genesis 9 names parties, promise, and sign after it.

rightEvidence.title: A covenant with Noah, descendants, and living creatures

payload.tension: The two sources materially share covenant language or memory, while their parties, setting, action, or literary purpose remain distinct.
payload.title: Announcement before danger / sign after danger
